rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honesty-alpha negative signal. The May 2026 Form 4 cluster (8 filings on 2026-05-15) is purely the annual director compensation grant calendar (all code A at $0), not conviction buying - a fact that becomes important because superficial Form-4-count screens often misread these as insider 'accumulation.' Director Roper's single 2025-05 code-P purchase at $33 has not been followed by ANY insider stepping in at the post-drawdown ~$18-19 range, including by the newly-installed CEO. Aggregated 24-month code-P:code-S dollar ratio is approximately 1:30 ($496K buy vs ~$15M+ sells in 2024-2025). This is the framework's 'absence-of-expected-buying' signal: when insiders sold heavily into the bad-news window and then nobody steps in to buy at the post-drawdown discount, the read-through is that the insiders themselves do not view the multi-segment whiskey-cycle thesis as a turn yet.

Both actions assert securities fraud claims under Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Exchange Act for the putative class who acquired publicly traded MGP common stock between May 4, 2023 and October 30, 2024.' rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - given securities class action existence (Mode A: confirmed via PACER docket), identify what the named defendants did during the class period that the issuer's risk factors do NOT explicitly admit: were the named former CEOs and current CFO transacting in MGPI stock during the class period, and is the new CEO appointment (Jul 21, 2025) a direct response?
rfm_tuples.M_source: form4 (parse insider transactions May 4, 2023 - Oct 30, 2024 class-period window) + edgar 8-K timeline (CEO transitions)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Two former CEOs are named defendants - corroborated by 8-K timeline: the company had at least two CEO transitions before settling on interim CFO Brandon Gall as interim CEO, then ultimately appointing outside-hire Julie Francis (ex-Schwan's COO, ex-Constellation Brands SVP Total Beverage Alcohol) on Jul 21, 2025. During the May 2023 - Oct 2024 alleged class period, insider sales by named/related parties: Karen Seaberg (then-Chair, founding-family principal stockholder, named 10% owner) sold over 1.47M shares for $65.0M lifetime through this period - including the Aug 23, 2024 $1.6M sell cluster at $90.67-$90.92 (peak share price); Lori Mingus and the Lux family trusts sold throughout 2024. The 10-K does not flag any accrual for the class-action loss contingency despite two consolidated complaints and named derivative actions; standard practice would be at least a directors-and-officers-insurance retention estimate. Penelope contingent consideration sits at $110.8M as a CURRENT liability at 3/31/2026 (Q1 10-Q confirms maximum earn-out target was achieved during the quarter), payable - i.e., the same Penelope acquisition the class-action complaints will probe was paid out at maximum just as the company recorded a separate $179.5M Q1 2026 impairment.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two active putative securities class actions + derivative suits + two consecutive ex-CEO defendants + a sitting CFO defendant + a brand-new outside CEO + zero quantitative loss-contingency accrual + a $110.8M Penelope earn-out maxing out concurrently with a $179.5M impairment of the same Branded Spirits segment that hosts Penelope - this is not isolated litigation, it is a structural multi-year disclosure-quality challenge. The framework's Mode-B catch here is that the disclosure existing is necessary but not sufficient: the issuer satisfies the 'we have litigation' Mode-A test, but Mode B requires that the magnitude, the named-defendant overlap with departed C-suite, and the simultaneous contradictory accounting outcome at Penelope (paying out the maximum earn-out while impairing the goodwill) be visible in one place, and they are not.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'Operating loss for 2025 was $(94,615), which decreased from operating income of $74,426 for 2024, primarily due to the $152,622 goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible asset impairment related to the Branded Spirits segment recorded during the fourth quarter 2025 ...' Q1 FY26 10-Q: 'Goodwill and other long-lived assets impairment 179,526 ... [in] the Branded Spirits segment.'
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check impairment cadence (2024 $73.8M Goodwill + 2025 $152.6M Goodwill+Intangibles + Q1 2026 $179.5M Goodwill+Long-Lived) against the disclosed cause (American-whiskey overhang) and against management's continued capital-allocation behavior (dividend $0.12/sh declared Feb 25, 2026 AND April 29, 2026; buyback authorization untouched $53.4M remaining).
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note on Goodwill - schedule with $247.789M -> $115.667M roll-forward; Q1 10-Q income statement)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Goodwill: $247.789M Dec 31 2024 -> $115.667M Dec 31 2025 (-$132.1M = -53.3% impairment of the carrying value in one year). Plus indefinite-lived intangibles impaired $20.5M in FY25 to total $152.6M of FY25 charges. Plus $179.5M further long-lived/goodwill impairment in Q1 FY26 (single quarter) on Branded Spirits - effectively the second wave eliminating most of the remaining Penelope/Branded Spirits carrying value. Cumulative 2024+2025+Q1-2026 impairments to Branded Spirits goodwill and intangibles: $73.8M + $152.6M + $179.5M = $405.9M. Yet the company (a) ratified payment of the Penelope contingent consideration at MAX ($110.8M, paid Q1/early Q2 FY26 per 10-Q subsequent events), (b) declared a $0.12/sh quarterly dividend on both 2026-02-25 (with the impairment-laden 10-K) and 2026-04-29 (with the $134.8M Q1 FY26 net loss 10-Q), (c) left buyback authorization at $53.4M open and unused, and (d) temporarily idled both Kentucky distilleries on 2026-04-07 while 'reaffirming' the full-year 2026 outlook.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Penelope acquisition (2023) is the single largest source of the impairment cascade; the company is simultaneously confessing in non-cash accounting that the asset is worth ~$406M less than they paid, while paying out the maximum cash earn-out to the seller because the contractual sales-volume hurdle was hit. That contradiction - earnout-hit-by-revenue-growth at the brand level while goodwill is destroyed by margin compression - implies the deal's pricing assumed both volume AND price/margin, and only volume showed up. Independently, declaring a dividend out of a $134.8M Q1 loss-quarter while idling both Kentucky distilleries is the classic 'maintain-the-prior-narrative' move flagged by the framework. The 10-K's risk-factor language and the Q1 10-Q MD&A both materially understate the magnitude of cumulative impairment relative to the dividend-maintenance signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A: 'Distilling Solutions segment sales for 2025 decreased 45 percent over the prior year ... During 2025, the industry continued to experience a softening of American whiskey category trends as well as elevated industry-wide barrel whiskey inventories, which resulted in the inability of some customers to honor their contracts with us and a number of our large customers to pause their whiskey purchases after completing their existing contracts. We expect these trends to continue.' 8-K 2026-04-07 (Item 7.01): 'the temporary idling of distilling operations at its two Kentucky distilleries and reaffirming the Company's full-year 2026 financial outlook.' Q1 FY26 MD&A: 'Within the Distilling Solutions segment, sales were down 40 percent primarily due to decreased sales of brown goods.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - given a 45% segment-sales collapse in 2025 PLUS a Q1 FY26 further 40% decline PLUS the announced May 2026 idling of BOTH Kentucky distilleries, verify whether the 'temporary' framing is structurally consistent with the company's customer-inability-to-honor-contracts language and elevated inventory state.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 1 + Item 7 + Item 8 Distilling Solutions disclosures; Q1 10-Q segment discussion; 8-K 2026-04-07 idling announcement; Bardstown feed-dryer abandonment in Q1 10-Q Note disclosure)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Distilling Solutions segment trajectory: 2024 sales declined 26% (Atchison Distillery closed Dec 2023), 2025 sales declined 45% on continued brown-goods softness, Q1 FY26 sales declined 40% with brown goods the primary driver. Customer-side disclosure language: 'inability of some customers to honor their contracts' (i.e., counterparty default on long-term whiskey contracts) and 'a number of our large customers to pause their whiskey purchases after completing their existing contracts.' Operational response: (a) Atchison Distillery already closed Dec 2023; (b) Bardstown, KY feed dryer abandoned in Q1 FY26 with $26.9M impairment ('does not intend to sell it'); (c) BOTH Kentucky distilleries (Lawrenceburg, IN is in Indiana - the 'two Kentucky distilleries' are Bardstown plus the Penelope distillery) idled effective immediately after 2026-04-07. The 'temporarily idling' + 'reaffirming the Company's full-year 2026 financial outlook' framing is internally inconsistent: idling both Kentucky distilleries shrinks the production base mid-year while management retains the same earnings outlook.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The combination of 45% YoY segment collapse + 40% sequential Q1 collapse + customer contract defaults + the company's own customers having barrel-inventory overhangs that prevent them from buying new + permanent feed-dryer abandonment + temporary distillery idling of BOTH remaining Kentucky facilities + ongoing dividend payments + reaffirmed outlook = a classic disclosure-pattern mismatch where the operational facts trend more negative than the financial-outlook framing. 'Temporary' is a managed word. The framework would treat the verbal hedge as overconfidence relative to the operational reality. This is the second tier of severity (along with the impairment cascade) supporting the SHORT-tier signal.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - given the Feb 11 2026 forced departures of two C-suite officers (CHRO + CCO) plus the cumulative leadership churn (two named ex-CEOs in the class-action complaints, Brandon Gall as interim CEO before Francis arrived Jul 2025, then Francis arriving as the first non-interim CEO in mid-2025), verify whether the disclosed 'reorganization' is consistent with the 10-K's restructuring language and whether severance liabilities are sized in the financials.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (8-K 2026-02-17 + 10-K Item 1 'restructuring actions' language) + form4 (timed Code-F tax-withholding sales by Lapish and Pasagic on 2026-02-14 and 2026-02-20, the dates straddling their announced departure)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Within ~6 months of new-CEO Francis's Jul 2025 arrival, two C-suite officers (CHRO Lapish, CCO Pasagic) are out by Feb 20, 2026 - immediately followed by the Feb 25, 2026 FY2025 earnings 8-K (with $152.6M impairment), then the Q1 FY26 $179.5M further impairment, then the Apr 7 distillery idling. CFO Gall remains but is a named defendant in the securities class action. The new CEO is also a director, getting her 150,000-share long-term-incentive grant on 2026-05-01 - i.e., the entire Form-4 cluster reflects compensation-mechanics, not conviction. Lapish and Pasagic's last Form-4s show forced code-F tax withholds at $25.74 and $25.93 - i.e., on the way out, they did not retain the post-vest shares but paid taxes via withhold; no further Form 4 from either after their separation dates. Severance: the 10-K does not pre-accrue severance but the 8-K notes Executive Severance Plan eligibility 'subject to compliance with the terms of the plan, including signing a release and agreeing to certain post-employment covenants' - i.e., conditioned, non-quantified.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Leadership churn pattern - 2 ex-CEOs (class-action defendants), interim CEO bridge, new CEO Jul 2025, 2 C-suite forced departures Feb 2026 - is itself a coherent restructuring story that the new CEO is executing on. The Mode-B finding is that the financial statements have not yet sized the cumulative severance/restructuring liability the 10-K hints at, and the new CEO has yet to put open-market personal capital behind the turnaround thesis. Not severe because turnarounds typically involve C-suite exits, but it is a real underdelivery relative to the calm 10-K narrative.

rfm_tuples.f: Mode A and Mode B - Mode A: dividend declarations actually filed. Mode B: given a -43.9% drawdown, $107.8M FY25 net loss, $134.8M Q1 FY26 net loss, idled distilleries, securities class action, and $110.8M Penelope earn-out paid out at max, why is the dividend being maintained, why is the $53.4M buyback authorization not being used at the post-drawdown price, and what does that signal about the company's actual liquidity confidence vs. its capital-return signaling priority?
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Item 5 + Note 16 + Q1 10-Q Note 10) + 10-K Item 7 'Cash Flow' section ($121.5M cash from ops in 2025; 'we anticipate that we will be able to meet the covenants in our credit arrangements, there can be no assurance that we will do so')
rfm_tuples.M_value: Operating cash flow $121.5M in 2025 (largely from the non-cash impairment add-back of $203.1M). Total debt $252.3M Dec 2025 (down from $323.5M Dec 2024 - principal pay-down + revolver from $105M to $42M; Q1 FY26 revolver further down to $36M). Convertible senior notes $201.25M (1.88% coupon due 2041, FV $195.5M vs face $201.3M). $0.12/sh quarterly dividend declared TWICE post-cutoff-period (Feb 25 and Apr 29 2026) totaling roughly $2.6M each quarter ($10.4M annualized) - sustained from FY25 dividend run-rate $10.7M ('dividends paid 10,659'). Buyback authorization $53.4M remaining: ZERO repurchases in FY25, $886K in Q1 FY26 (essentially tax-withhold-related, not opportunistic). The company prefers to pay an unchanged dividend over deploying the buyback authorization to retire shares at the post-drawdown discount - which is the OPPOSITE of what a management with conviction would do at a -44% price.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The dividend maintenance is the textbook 'optical-signal capital return' that diverts attention from the operating reality. The clean Mode-B catch is the asymmetry: ample buyback capacity ($53.4M open authorization) is left unused while a smaller dividend is preserved - the rational order is reversed if management believed the equity were undervalued. The framework reads this as low management conviction in the share price relative to its preference for being seen as a continuing dividend payer. Liquidity is not stressed (operating cash flow positive, total debt reducing) so this is moderate not severe, but the signal is real.

rfm_tuples.R: Q1 10-Q Note disclosure: 'There was no adjustment to the fair value of the contingent consideration liability during the quarter ended March 31, 2026, as the Company achieved the maximum net sales target as defined ...' Balance sheet 2026-03-31: 'Contingent consideration 110,800' as CURRENT liability (vs $110,800 at Dec 31 2025 but reclassified to current). 10-K Note: 'Penelope acquisition' contingent-consideration earnout uses Monte Carlo simulation on net sales over the earn-out period.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B - reconcile two contradictory facts: (a) Penelope's contractual NET SALES earn-out hit its MAXIMUM target, AND (b) the company recorded a $179.5M Q1 FY26 goodwill/long-lived-asset impairment to the Branded Spirits segment (which contains Penelope). Verify whether the 10-Q disaggregates impairment by reporting unit and whether Penelope per-unit margins are now negative.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (Q1 10-Q Note + 10-K Note on Penelope acquisition + Goodwill roll-forward)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Penelope acquired June 1, 2023 for cash + contingent consideration earn-out. Earn-out is volume-based (net sales targets) and was BOOKED at $110.8M (maximum). Maximum was earned during Q1 FY26 - i.e., volume target met. Concurrently, Branded Spirits goodwill went from $247.8M (Dec 24) to $115.7M (Dec 25) - $132.1M impairment - and the company took another $179.5M of impairment in Q1 FY26 ($26.9M of which is the explicitly disclosed Bardstown feed-dryer abandonment, with the remaining $152.6M presumably goodwill/trade-name impairment in Branded Spirits). The framework's Mode-B catch: max earn-out hitting AND max goodwill impairment in the SAME quarter on the SAME segment means the deal achieved volume but the implicit price/margin/discount-rate assumptions in the 2023 purchase price are now in tatters. The seller gets paid at the max ($110.8M cash out), the buyer carries a cumulative $400M+ accounting hole on the asset, and the company funds the maximum earn-out payment from a revolver that has been actively drawn down. Penelope distillery is now one of the two Kentucky distilleries being temporarily idled per the Apr 7 8-K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the single sharpest Mode-B finding in the file. The bargaining structure of the Penelope deal (volume-only earn-out) has produced a worst-of-both-worlds outcome at the cyclical bottom: the company owes the max cash payment, owns a brand whose carrying value is being written to near-zero, and is shutting the production facility for the brand. The 10-K and 10-Q both technically disclose each of these facts in separate sections but never in juxtaposition. The earn-out payment will hit cash in Q2 FY26 - i.e., a $110.8M cash use that the dividend-maintenance narrative has not had to contend with yet.

supplemental_signals.honesty_alpha_frame: MGPI's disclosure is largely complete and on time - the company is NOT a liar in the SRPT/AHC sense. But honesty-alpha is about excluding the over-confident; here the over-confidence is dividend-maintenance and 'reaffirmed outlook' language at the same moment as the second consecutive 9-figure quarterly impairment and the temporary idling of the remaining distillery base. The cumulative R/f/M severity grid is SEVERE x 3 + RED_FLAG x 2 + MODERATE x 2 = bottom-quartile.

summary: MGPI fits the framework's SHORT-tier honesty-alpha pattern despite reasonable on-time disclosure. Three SEVERE underdeliveries (Penelope earn-out paid at max concurrent with $405.9M cumulative Branded Spirits impairment cascade; securities class action with 2 ex-CEO + CFO defendants and no accrual; 45% then 40% YoY Distilling Solutions collapse with temporary idling of BOTH remaining Kentucky distilleries while reaffirming the outlook). Two RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE signals from Form 4: zero 2026 open-market code-P purchases at -44% drawdown despite director Roper's pre-drawdown $496K buy at $33 (post-drawdown silence is the strongest negative tell), and clustered post-class-period selling by founder-family principal stockholders ($65M lifetime by Seaberg alone, $13M by Donn Lux, plus extended-trust sellers). Two MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY items (leadership churn / cost-rationalization; dividend-maintenance + unused buyback). Verdict: SHORT-tier. The new CEO Julie Francis (appointed Jul 21, 2025) has yet to put personal open-market capital behind the turnaround thesis through May 15, 2026.
